root_cause_hypothesis: Windows child profile isolation is incomplete: M5 ProcessEnvironment does not set USERPROFILE while multiple Godot processes are launched concurrently/sequentially.
Current M5 parent harness waits only on JSON state and does not fail fast when a child process dies, making early process death indistinguishable from later orchestration/state failure.
The instability may still be deeper than profile/lifecycle harnessing; therefore the first repair must improve observability without changing gameplay semantics.
r1_changes: Add USERPROFILE and explicit inventory-profile isolation to each M5 child process profile.
Add fail-fast child-process liveness checks to M5 state waits and preserve the last observed report plus wait label on early death.
Add a deterministic Windows stability runner that executes the same standalone M5 acceptance 10 times and stops/preserves on first failure.
non_goals: Do not increase M5 timeouts as the primary fix.
Do not add automatic reruns to RUN_WORLD_REGRESSION_TESTS.ps1.
Do not weaken M5 assertions or convergence semantics.
Do not change SM1 runtime or its already-reviewed candidate.
Do not claim environment root cause unless the repaired harness evidence supports it.
acceptance_r1: Standalone M5 graphical acceptance passes 10 consecutive first-attempt runs on the Windows verifier machine.
No hidden rerun after a failure.
Each run has isolated child profiles and no profile-collision/editor-settings crash markers.
If a child dies, the harness reports which process/wait stage died instead of only a generic timeout/exit -1.
After 10/10 M5 stability, rerun canonical RUN_WORLD_REGRESSION_TESTS.ps1 once from a fresh checkout of the repaired candidate.
escalation_rule: If R1 still fails, preserve the first failing run and create R2 from the new lifecycle evidence. Do not patch M5 gameplay/runtime semantics without a second Repair Map identifying a canonical root cause.
